definitions.gloss: competitive spirit; fighting spirit; refusal to be beaten
definitions.explanation: The temperament of someone who hates losing and pushes back rather than giving in. Usually admiring, though it can hint at stubbornness.

examples.japanese: {弟|おとうと}は{昔|むかし}から{負|ま}けん{気|き}の{強|つよ}い{子|こ}だった。
examples.english: My younger brother has always been a child who couldn't stand losing.

examples.japanese: {負|ま}けん{気|き}を{出|だ}して{練習|れんしゅう}を{続|つづ}けたおかげで、{最後|さいご}には{代表|だいひょう}に{選|えら}ばれた。
examples.english: Thanks to summoning up her competitive spirit and keeping at her training, she was chosen for the national team in the end.

notes:
From {負|ま}ける (to lose) with the old negative ん: literally "the spirit of not losing."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {負|ま}けん{気|き}が{強|つよ}い: to have a strong competitive streak (the standard phrase)
- {負|ま}けん{気|き}の{強|つよ}い{性格|せいかく}: a competitive personality
- {負|ま}けん{気|き}を{出|だ}す: to summon up one's fighting spirit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {向|む}こう{気|き}: pluck, combativeness — readiness to take someone on, with less of the hatred of losing
- {根性|こんじょう}: guts, perseverance — about enduring hardship rather than beating a rival
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}り: stubbornness — the same refusal to yield, but plainly negative
